content:
According to NBC News reports, Apple's negotiations with OpenAI over alleged theft of trade secrets have broken down, after Apple's external lawyers accidentally sent an email to the wrong OpenAI employee, mixing up the two parties' communications. Details of the incident are as follows.

The report pointed out that Apple's external legal counsel mixed up the two email recipients.

Last Friday, Apple filed a trade secret theft lawsuit against OpenAI Products and two former employees, Chang Liu and Tang Tan.

Apple alleged in the lawsuit that its former employees stole confidential hardware information to advance OpenAI's consumer device business.

Apple claimed that when it first raised the issue directly with OpenAI in February this year, OpenAI did not respond:

However, according to NBC News, OpenAI said it had responded to Apple's initial outreach, but the communications subsequently broke down after Apple's external lawyer sent an email to the wrong OpenAI employee, mixing up the recipients.

The report pointed out that Gabriel Gross of Apple's external law firm Weil, Gotshal & Manges sent an email to OpenAI's general counsel Che Chang, with the subject 'Former Apple employees retained non-public, confidential and proprietary information at OpenAI,' and attached supporting documents for Apple's allegations.

Thirteen minutes later, Gross sent another email to Chang, thanking him for taking time to take a phone call and for 'quickly expressing willingness to cooperate.'

The problem was that the second email was not meant for Chang, but was written to 'a former Apple employee surnamed Wang who had jumped ship to OpenAI,' NBC News pointed out. Gross had previously sent emails to Chang and Mr. Wang separately, and had also spoken to Mr. Wang by phone in between, but when replying, he mixed up the recipients and mistakenly sent the email to Chang.

Chang believed that Gross had sent him fabricated information to advance Apple's case against OpenAI, so he contacted two of Apple's in-house lawyers, accusing the company's external counsel of 'falsely claiming to have spoken to me on the phone,' and added: 'I don't know him, we have never spoken.' Chang subsequently demanded that Gross be replaced.

Gross subsequently apologized to Chang, and one of Apple's in-house lawyers also told Chang that he could continue to communicate with Gross and his law firm during the litigation process. NBC News pointed out that 'the negotiations appear to have ended there,' and added that OpenAI claimed 'there is no record of any contact from any Apple lawyers before Apple filed the lawsuit last Friday.'
